SOC 2 / ISO 27001 scope and evidence requests
transcript:
[00:00:00] Nina Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about an hour. Quick intro, I'm Nina, AE on the Redwood team, Marcus is our SE.
[00:00:10] Marcus Li: hi all, Marcus here, I'll focus on the IdP/SCIM bits and role mapping.
[00:00:20] Aisha Khan: hey, Aisha from Stratus. We wanted to walk through how Redwood expects SAML and SCIM to be wired, and how to enforce least privilege at the route/model level.
[00:00:35] Marcus Li: sure, good call. At a high level we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. Typical flow is exchange metadata (IdP metadata file), configure assertions for groups, then SCIM pushes groups to Redwood's user directory.
[00:00:55] Tom Reynolds: quick question — how do you handle cert rotation? We rotate our IdP certs every 90 days.
[00:01:05] Marcus Li: we allow multiple active certs during rollover windows, and our console accepts new metadata uploads. There is also an API endpoint to rotate programmatically. Note, in Private deployments you can bring your own KMS and HSM, so certs and keys never leave your boundary.
[00:01:28] Marta Silva: on SCIM, can we send filters? we don't want service accounts from the dev orgs to end up as Redwood admins.
[00:01:37] Marcus Li: absolutely, SCIM group filters are supported — you can map SCIM groups to Redwood roles and apply regex-style filters or prefix rules. We usually recommend a 'role-slice' approach where you define minimal role slices per capability: viewer, runner, model-deployer, billing-auditor.
[00:02:00] Ben O'Connor: role-slice, interesting phrasing. so each slice is a narrow permission set and you compose them?
[00:02:08] Marcus Li: yes, exactly. Compose slices to build job-specific roles rather than umbrella roles. That helps with least privilege and auditability.
[00:02:22] Aisha Khan: how do you audit which API key or user invoked a model? we need per-call audit logs for compliance.
[00:02:31] Nina Patel: good one — Redwood Console exposes per-token and per-request tracing. Logs include request id, caller principal (SCIM user or API key), model and route, latency, and token counts. We can stream logs to your SIEM or S3 and keep a retention policy per-tenant.
[00:02:51] Tom Reynolds: what about retention durations and exports for legal hold?
[00:02:56] Marcus Li: hosted customers get configurable retention up to X days by default — we can push longer retention as a paid add-on or recommend Private deployment for long-term on-prem retention. We also support on-demand snapshots of logs for e-discovery.
[00:03:12] Marta Silva: encryption question — keys in transit and at rest, and KMS integration.
[00:03:18] Marcus Li: TLS in transit everywhere. At rest we use envelope encryption. For hosted we manage KMS but provide customer-managed keys (CMK) options via partner KMS; for Private you plug into your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp HSM) and we never see plaintext.
[00:03:36] Ben O'Connor: do you support customer HSM-backed EKM for FIPS 140-2?
[00:03:41] Marcus Li: yes for Private we support HSM-backed keys and FIPS workflows. For hosted, we can offer HSM protected CMKs on an enterprise contract.
[00:03:52] Aisha Khan: SOC 2 and ISO — we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope. can you share those artifacts?
[00:03:59] Nina Patel: yes, happy to. I'll send the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and our ISO 27001 statement of applicability and scope. We'll also include our pen test summary and compliance pack.
[00:04:13] Tom Reynolds: great. operationally, if we want to test SCIM mapping, can we get a sandbox tenant?
[00:04:19] Nina Patel: yes, we can provision a sandbox environment with a test IdP and sample data. Marcus, can we do a test exchange?
[00:04:26] Marcus Li: for sure. Typical steps: 1) customer exports IdP metadata, 2) we import into Redwood sandbox, 3) we configure assertion mappings (email, name, groups), 4) SCIM push and verify groups appear, 5) validate role mapping and policy enforcement.
[00:04:46] Marta Silva: for group-to-role mapping — we have nested groups and some cross-org shared groups. any gotchas?
[00:04:55] Marcus Li: nested groups can be flattened in the SCIM layer; we have options to expand membership. For shared groups we recommend prefixing and using deny-lists for sensitive admin roles. Also recommend test runs to ensure service accounts aren't automatically elevated.
[00:05:12] Ben O'Connor: network connectivity — if we go Private, how does traffic path look and is there VPC peering or transit gateway support?
[00:05:20] Marcus Li: Private supports VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on region. We can support Transit Gateway for scale. We also offer a hybrid routing mode for dedicated where control plane is separated from data plane.
[00:05:36] Tom Reynolds: about tracing: do you sample traces or is every call captured?
[00:05:41] Nina Patel: by default, we capture structured logs for every call (request id, tokens, latency) but full debug traces are sampled to control overhead. Sampling is configurable per-route in the Console.
[00:05:55] Aisha Khan: any limitations on SCIM attributes? we rely on custom attributes like cost_center and env_tag.
[00:06:02] Marcus Li: SCIM supports custom extension attributes; we map them into user profile fields and can use them in attribute-based access policies.
[00:06:14] Marta Silva: what about emergency access — break-glass?
[00:06:18] Marcus Li: we recommend a break-glass workflow using short-lived session tokens with MFA, logged and flagged in audit logs, and an approval workflow. For Private we can integrate with your privileged access manager.
[00:06:33] Ben O'Connor: latency impact with encryption and private endpoints?
[00:06:38] Marcus Li: small delta; most latency comes from network hop. Private with same-region hosting keeps latency minimal. Our runtime optimizes tokenization and KV cache so cryptographic overhead is negligible.
[00:06:50] Tom Reynolds: any known gaps vs providers like Okta/Auth0?
[00:06:54] Nina Patel: we cover core SSO/SCIM needs similar to IdP vendors, but we focus on model-level RBAC and per-token cost telemetry which is unique. For deep IdP lifecycle features you might keep Okta as master IdP and use SCIM to sync into Redwood.
[00:07:10] Aisha Khan: recap and next steps?
[00:07:14] Nina Patel: we'll send the compliance pack, Marcus will draft the SCIM mapping and role-slice examples, customer will share IdP metadata and role matrix, and we'll schedule the SE-led test in early July.
[00:07:27] Marta Silva: thanks everyone, that's helpful.
[00:07:30] Marcus Li: thanks, bye.
[00:07:32] (call ends)
